function.name: see_build
function.description: Screenshot the build as Minecraft makes it: the engine places your blocks (shapes, connections, blocks that cannot stay) and runs ticks (water and lava flow, sand falls, scheduled ticks fire), then renders it. A shot's tick is how many ticks the build has run (default: the ticks of the last build's settle; 0 is as placed, at most ⟦simulationTicks⟧); shots at different ticks in one call show several moments of one run. The result says, for each tick shown, which block ids Minecraft removed, added or replaced against your blueprint. Each shot is saved under /work/images (its path is in the result) for bash and view_image. Use test_build for redstone behavior.

view.description: Named view of the framed blocks (default iso_se). front looks from the south, back from the north, left from the east, right from the west, top straight down with north up.

eye.description: Your own camera position, with target, instead of view.

region.description: Blocks to frame (default: everything drawn). Not with a perspective eye.

clip.description: Draw only the blocks inside this box: cut away roofs, walls or neighbours to see interiors and sections. To see into a room, end the box inside the roof and inside the walls that face the camera.

projection.description: orthographic: parallel projection, true plans and elevations (default perspective).

fov.description: Perspective field of view in degrees, 5 to 120 (default 70). Smaller zooms in.

grid.description: Block grid with coordinate labels. Orthographic top, front, back, left or right only.

tick.description: Ticks the build has run when this shot is taken (default: the last build's settle ticks).

attach.description: false: only save the shots under /work/images, without adding them to your context (default true).
